## Module Objectives

At the end of this module, you should be able to:

- Collaborate effectively on data science projects using `GitHub`.
- Ensure the reproducibility of analyzes with `Quarto`.
- Merge and manage multiple datasets.
- Explain the data life cycle and the principles of `DataOps`.

<h3 class="unnumbered" id="challenge-cross-review-of-logbooks">Challenge — Cross-review of logbooks</h3>
<blockquote>
<p>Each team must <strong>share their logbook</strong> with another team and provide <strong>constructive feedback</strong>. This step simulates the peer review process and reinforces critical communication skills.</p>
</blockquote>
<h4 id="steps-to-take">Steps to take</h4>
<ol type="1">
<li><p><strong>Assignment of pairs</strong>: the teacher will publish a table listing for each team the logbook to be examined.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Sharing the document</strong>:</p>
<ul>
<li>The repository manager adds the recipient team as a read/write <em>Collaborator</em> on GitHub.</li>
<li>The URL of the HTML logbook is communicated.</li>
</ul></li>
<li><p><strong>Peer Review</strong>:</p>
<ul>
<li><p>Each member of the review team opens an <em>Issue</em> in the review team repository and submits at least <strong>one detailed comment</strong> relating to:</p>
<ol type="1">
<li><strong>Clarity</strong> of content (structure, titles, readability)</li>
<li><strong>Rigour</strong> of the methodology (description of roles, reproducibility of the code)</li>
<li><strong>Relevance</strong> of reflections (data life cycle, lessons learned)</li>
</ol></li>
<li><p>Comments must contain:</p>
<ul>
<li>A positive aspect statement (“what is successful”)</li>
<li>A specific suggestion for improvement (“what could be clarified”)</li>
</ul></li>
</ul></li>
<li><p><strong>Acknowledgement of receipt &amp; review</strong>:</p>
<ul>
<li>The receiving team responds to each <em>Issue</em> and, if deemed necessary, updates its logbook.</li>
</ul></li>
</ol>
<h4 id="deliverables">Deliverables</h4>
<table style="width:100%;">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 22%" />
<col style="width: 54%" />
<col style="width: 22%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Team</th>
<th>Deliverable</th>
<th>Where to drop it off</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><strong>Reviewing team</strong></td>
<td>≥ 3 <em>Issues</em> (one per member) containing full feedback</td>
<td>GitHub repository of the reviewed team</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Revised team</strong></td>
<td>Updated logbook (if necessary modifications) + responses to <em>Issues</em></td>
<td>Same GitHub repository</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<h4 id="scale-20pts">Scale (20pts)</h4>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 85%" />
<col style="width: 14%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Criterion</th>
<th>Pts</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Quality of comments (clarity, constructiveness, examples)</td>
<td>10</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Relevance of suggestions to reproducibility &amp; collaboration</td>
<td>5</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Follow-up and responses from the revised team</td>
<td>5</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<hr />
<blockquote>
<p><strong>Tip</strong>: focus on actionable feedback (e.g. proposing a more descriptive title, adding an additional graphic, specifying a YAML parameter) rather than generic comments.</p>
</blockquote>
